text:
William Nylander scored his 300th career goal, and the Maple Leafs used the night to end Edmonton's three-game winning streak in the most lopsided way available. Toronto won 7-2 at Rogers Place for its fourth straight win, with Nylander adding a second goal late for good measure. Anthony Stolarz, a second-round pick of the Flyers in 2012 who spent 47 AHL games in Lehigh Valley before reaching the NHL, was named the game's first star in goal.

The scoreboard flatters Toronto, though, and our numbers say so plainly. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of goals, came out nearly even: 3.02 for Edmonton, 2.99 for Toronto. By our deserved-to-win measure (the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins), the Oilers would have taken it 59 percent of the time. They out-attempted the Leafs 68 to 59 and owned the first period, 1.19 expected goals to 0.45. Toronto still led 1-0 after Jack Roslovic scored on a chance worth just 4 percent.

The gap came in net. Stolarz stopped 30 of 32 shots and saved just over one goal more than the chances against him should have allowed. Tristan Jarry allowed six on 31 shots, about 3.5 more than the quality of those shots deserved, and Edmonton fell behind 3-0 on two goals in 54 seconds of the second period. Leon Draisaitl scored twice, but the Oilers never got closer than three. Toronto has won four straight; Edmonton's three-game run is over.
